parts.title: Vol 16-Section 3
parts.passageHtml:
{[Norman M. Weinberger reviews the latest work of Oliver Sacks on music.][302214]}

{[Music and the brain are both endlessly fascinating subjects, and as a neuroscientist specialising in auditory learning and memory, I find them especially intriguing.][302228]} {[So I had high expectations of Musicophilia, the latest offering from neurologist and prolific author Oliver Sacks.][302252]} {[And I confess to feeling a little guilty reporting that my reactions to the book are mixed.][302270]}

{[Sacks himself is the best part of Musicophilia.][302290]} {[He richly documents his own life in the book and reveals highly personal experiences.][302299]} {[The photograph of him on the cover of the book— which shows him wearing headphones, eyes closed, clearly enchanted as he listens to Alfred Brendel perform Beethoven’s Pathétique Sonata—makes a positive impression that is borne out by the contents of the book.][302314]} {[Sacks’s voice throughout is steady and erudite but never pontifical.][302357]} {[He is neither self-conscious nor self-promoting.][302368]}

{[The preface gives a good idea of what the book will deliver.][302376]} {[In it Sacks explains that he wants to convey the insights gleaned from the “enormous and rapidly growing body of work on the neural underpinnings of musical perception and imagery, and the complex and often bizarre disorders to which these are prone” He also stresses the importance of “the simple art of observation” and “the richness of the human context.][302388]} {[” He wants to combine “observation and description with the latest in technology,” he says, and to imaginatively enter into the experience of his patients and subjects.][302454]} {[The reader can see that Sacks, who has been practicing neurology for 40 years, is torn between the “old-fashioned” path of observation and the new-fangled, high-tech approach: He knows that he needs to take heed of the latter, but his heart lies with the former.][302481]}

{[The book consists mainly of detailed descriptions of cases, most of them involving patients whom Sacks has seen in his practice.][302522]} {[Brief discussions of contemporary neuroscientific reports are sprinkled liberally throughout the text.][302543]} {[Part I, “Haunted by Music,” begins with the strange case of Tony Cicoria, a nonmusical, middle-aged surgeon who was consumed by a love of music after being hit by lightning.][302556]} {[He suddenly began to crave listening to piano music, which he had never cared for in the past.][302586]} {[He started to play the piano and then to compose music, which arose spontaneously in his mind in a “torrent” of notes.][302605]} {[How could this happen?][302626]} {[Was the cause psychological?][302631]} {[(He had had a near-death experience when the lightning struck him. )][302636]} {[Or was it the direct result of a change in the auditory regions of his cerebral cortex?][302650]} {[Electro encephalography (EEG) showed his brain waves to be normal in the mid-1990s, just after his trauma and subsequent “conversion” to music.][302666]} {[There are now more sensitive tests, but Cicoria has declined to undergo them; he does not want to delve into the causes of his musicality.][302690]} {[What a shame!][302716]}

{[Part II, “A Range of Musicality,” covers a wider variety of topics, but unfortunately, some of the chapters offer little or nothing that is new.][302720]} {[For example, chapter 13, which is five pages long, merely notes that the blind often have better hearing than the sighted.][302743]} {[The most interesting chapters are those that present the strangest cases.][302765]} {[Chapter 8 is about “amusia,” an inability to hear sounds as music, and “dysharmonia,” a highly specific impairment of the ability to hear harmony, with the ability to understand melody left intact.][302777]} {[Such specific “dissociations” are found throughout the cases Sacks recounts.][302808]}

{[To Sacks’s credit, part III, “Memory, Movement and Music,” brings us into the underappreciated realm of music therapy.][302820]} {[Chapter 16 explains how “melodic intonation therapy” is being used to help expressive aphasic patients (those unable to express their thoughts verbally following a stroke or other cerebral incident) once again become capable of fluent speech.][302839]} {[In chapter 20, Sacks demonstrates the near-miraculous power of music to animate Parkinson’s patients and other people with severe movement disorders, even those who are frozen into odd postures.][302876]} {[Scientists cannot yet explain how music achieves this effect.][302906]}

{[To readers who are unfamiliar with neuroscience and music behavior, Musicophilia may be something of a revelation.][302917]} {[But the book will not satisfy those seeking the causes and implications of the phenomena Sacks describes.][302934]} {[For one thing, Sacks appears to be more at ease discussing patients than discussing experiments.][302952]} {[And he tends to be rather uncritical in accepting scientific findings and theories.][302968]}

{[It’s true that the causes of music-brain oddities remain poorly understood.][302983]} {[However, Sacks could have done more to draw out some of the implications of the careful observations that he and other neurologists have made and of the treatments that have been successful.][302994]} {[For example, he might have noted that the many specific dissociations among components of music comprehension, such as loss of the ability to perceive harmony but not melody, indicate that there is no music center in the brain.][303027]} {[Because many people who read the book are likely to believe in the brain localisation of all mental functions, this was a missed educational opportunity.][303066]}

{[Another conclusion one could draw is that there seem to be no “cures” for neurological problems involving music.][303092]} {[A drug can alleviate a symptom in one patient and aggravate it in another, or can have both positive and negative effects in the same patient.][303111]} {[Treatments mentioned seem to be almost exclusively antiepileptic medications, which “damp down” the excitability of the brain in general; their effectiveness varies widely.][303135]}

{[Finally, in many of the cases described here the patient with music-brain symptoms is reported to have “normal” EEG results.][303160]} {[Although Sacks recognises the existence of new technologies, among them far more sensitive ways to analyze brain waves than the standard neurological EEG test, he does not call for their use.][303181]} {[In fact, although he exhibits the greatest compassion for patients, he conveys no sense of urgency about the pursuit of new avenues in the diagnosis and treatment of music-brain disorders.][303213]} {[This absence echoes the hook’s preface, in which Sacks expresses fear that “the simple art of observation may be lost” if we rely too much on new technologies.][303244]} {[He does call for both approaches, though, and we can only hope that the neurological community will respond.][303273]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 4:

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

Write the correct letter in boxes 1-4 on your answer sheet.

options.text: The guilty feeling made him so.
The writer expected it to be better than it was.
Sacks failed to include his personal stories in the book.
This is the only book written by Sacks.

questions.explanationHtml:
B
Trong bài đọc, Norman (tác giả bài viết) đã kỳ vọng rất lớn vào cuốn sách Musicophilia vì cuốn sách được viết bởi nhà thần kinh học, tác giả nổi tiếng Oliver Sacks. Tuy nhiên tác giả thú thật rằng cảm thấy hơi "tội lỗi" vì nhận xét của ông về cuốn sách không được tốt lắm.
​
* Thông thường khi mình nói về "mixed feelings" hoặc "mixed reactions" là mình nói việc gì đó chưa thuyết phục

options.text: the photo of Sacks listening to music
the tone of voice of the book
the autobiographical description in the book
the description of Sacks’s wealth

questions.explanationHtml:
C
"Sacks himself is the best part of Musicophilia" => Bản thân và cuộc đời của Sacks là phần thú vị nhất của sách Musicophilia.
​
C: "the autobiographical description in the book" => phần tự truyện trong cuốn sách.

options.text: make terms with the new technologies
give detailed description of various musical disorders
explain how people understand music
explain why he needs to do away with simple observation

questions.explanationHtml:
A
​
Câu hỏi: Trong phần mở đầu (in the preface) của cuốn sách, Sacks nói đến vấn đề mà ông muốn đạt được là gì? 
 
Trong bài đọc, ông ấy muốn kết hợp việc quan sát và mô tả (observation and description) các biểu hiện của bệnh nhân với công nghệ mới nhất (the latest in technology) .
​
A: make terms with the new technologies = hiểu được (make terms with) các công nghệ mới.

options.text: He refuses to have further tests.
He can’t determine the cause of his sudden musicality.
He nearly died because of the lightening.
His brain waves were too normal to show anything.

questions.explanationHtml:
A
​
Trong bài đọc, anh ấy từ chối các bài Tests mới, việc này theo tác giả là 1 sự thất vọng lớn (What a shame!), bởi vì, các bài Tests này được cho là nhạy hơn (more sensitive tests) có khả năng sẽ giải thích được việc tại sao Cicoria lại bắt đầu yêu thích âm nhạc và bắt đầu chơi piano sau khi bị sét đánh trúng (after being hit by lightning).
 
=>A He refuses to have further tests.

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 5 - 10:

Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 3?

In boxes 5-10 on your answer sheet, write

YES                 if the statement agrees with the views of the writer

NO                  if the statement contradicts the views of the writer

NOT GIVEN   if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this

options.text: YES
NO
NOT GIVEN

questions.text: It is difficult to give a well-reputable writer a less than favorable review.
questions.explanationHtml:
Yes
Trong bài đọc, Norman đã kỳ vọng rất nhiều vào cuốn sách Musicophilia vì cuốn sách được viết bởi nhà thần kinh học, tác giả nổi tiếng Oliver Sacks. Tuy nhiên tác giả thú thật rằng cảm thấy hơi "tội lỗi" vì nhận xét của ông về cuốn sách không được tốt lắm.
​
* Thông thường khi mình nói về "mixed feelings" hoặc "mixed reactions" là mình nói việc gì đó chưa thuyết phục.
 
Câu 5 nhận định: Việc đánh giá không tốt về 1 cuốn sách được viết bởi 1 tác giả nổi tiếng là 1 việc rất khó khăn. => Tương tự với ý trong bài => YES

questions.text: Beethoven’s Pathétique Sonata is a good treatment for musical disorders.
questions.explanationHtml:
Nhận định của câu 6: Bản giao hưởng Pathétique Sonata của Beethoven là "1 cách chữa trị tốt" (a good treatment) cho hội chứng "musical disorders", ý nói là các bệnh nhân khi nghe bản giao hưởng này sẽ cải thiện được tình trạng bênh của mình.
 
Trong phần highlight, có nói đến việc có những người không nghe được "harmony", nhưng mà tiếp nhận được "melody" => musical disorders
 
Tuy nhiên, phần này không đề cập đến việc nghe các bản giao hưởng của Beethoven có cải thiện được tình trạng bệnh hay không. =>Not Given

questions.text: Sacks believes technological methods is not important compared with observation when studying his patients.
questions.explanationHtml:
No
​
Trong bài đọc, ông ấy biết là mình cần tìm hiểu/lưu ý về các công nghệ mới.
TAKE HEED = nên lưu ý, tìm hiểu.
​
7/ Sacks believes technological methods is not important compared with observation when studying his patients. =>câu 7 nói là Sacks thấy công nghệ mới không quan trọng => NO

questions.text: It is difficult to understand why music therapy is undervalued.
questions.explanationHtml:
Câu 8:

1. Dịch câu hỏi: Rất khó để hiểu tại sao liệu pháp âm nhạc bị đánh giá thấp.

2. Locate: các cụm trong câu hỏi được paraphrase tương ứng trong bài là:

"music therapy" (liệu pháp âm nhạc) ~ giống thông tin trong bài

"undervalued" (đánh giá thấp) ~ "underappreciated" (không được trân trọng)

3. Giải thích: Bài chỉ đề cập rằng liệu pháp âm nhạc không được trân trọng-đánh giá cao- (underappreciated), nhưng không đề cập đến việc để hiểu được việc này là có khó hay không.

4. Đáp án: NOT GIVEN

questions.text: Sacks should have more skepticism about other theories and findings.
questions.explanationHtml:
Yes
Trong bài đọc, "he tends to be uncritical in accepting scientific findings and theories" => ông ấy thường có xu hướng dễ tính trong việc chấp nhận các báo cáo và kết quả nghiên cứu khoa học. Ý của tác giả  là Sacks nên khó tính hơn trong việc chấp nhận quan điểm này.
 
Câu 9: nói là Sacks nên có nhiều "sự hoài nghi" (skepticism) về những lý thuyết và nghiên cứu khác. => Đúng với ý trong bài.

questions.text: Sacks is impatient to use new testing methods.
questions.explanationHtml:
No
​
Trong bài đọc, "he conveys no sense of urgency about the pursuit of new avenues in the diagnosis and treatment of music-brain disorders" =>ông ấy không thể hiện sự quyết liệt/ sự gấp rút trong việc theo đuổi các phương pháp chẩn đoán mới.
​
 "Sacks is impatient to use new testing methods." => câu hỏi thì lại nói là ông ấy nôn nóng trong việc dùng các phương pháp kiểm tra mới
​
=>NO

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 11 - 14:

Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A-F, below.

Write the correct letter, A-F, in boxes 11-14 on your answer sheet.

A    show no music-brain disorders.

B    indicates that medication can have varied results.

C    is key for the neurological community to unravel the mysteries.

D    should not be used in isolation.

E    indicate that not everyone can receive good education.

F    show that music is not localised in the brain.
questionSets.contentHtml:
A    show no music-brain disorders.

B    indicates that medication can have varied results.

C    is key for the neurological community to unravel the mysteries.

D    should not be used in isolation.

E    indicate that not everyone can receive good education.

F    show that music is not localised in the brain.

The dissociations between harmony and melody 11

The study of treating musical disorders 12

The EEG scans of Sacks’s patients 13

Sacks believes testing based on new technologies 14

options.text: A
B
C
D
E
F

questions.explanationHtml:
F
Trong bài đọc, nói là không có "trung tâm" cảm thụ nhạc trên não, bởi vì 1 người có thể mất khả năng cảm thụ sự hòa hợp trong âm nhạc nhưng vẫn có khả năng cảm thụ giai điệu.
=>37 + F : The dissociations between harmony and melody show that music is not localised in the brain. => sự "phân ly" (không liên quan) giữa "sự hòa hợp" và "giai điệu" cho thấy là âm nhạc không có "trung tâm"/"localised" ở não.
